rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Band theory explains conductivity through allowed energy bands, gaps and carrier availability. Thermal and optical excitation can create mobile electron–hole pairs.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Band gap Eg=Ec−Ev.
Photon excitation: hν≥Eg; threshold wavelength λ≤hc/Eg.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: A band gap is a forbidden energy range, not a physical gap in the material.  ·  Band gap alone does not determine conductivity without carrier concentration and mobility.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Allowed bands and forbidden gaps arise in the periodic solid.  ·  Carrier concentration and mobility jointly determine conductivity.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: For Eg=2.0 eV, λthreshold≈1240/2.0=620 nm.  ·  Thermal promotion across the gap creates one conduction electron and one valence-band hole.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: A symbol is not a number until the unit is named.  ·  A proportional relation is not an equality until the constant is included.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Compare band diagrams for metal, semiconductor and insulator.  ·  Find threshold wavelength for Eg=1.5 eV using hc≈1240 eV·nm.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Why can heating an intrinsic semiconductor increase conductivity?

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: An electron promoted to conduction leaves a hole.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: A conductor has overlapping or partly filled bands  ·  An insulator has a large gap. A semiconductor has a smaller gap  ·  Convert units before substituting.  ·  Quote the unit with the result.

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: In a solid the atomic levels spread into bands. A conductor has a partly filled band, or overlapping bands, so electrons can take a little extra energy and move. An insulator has a full valence band and a large gap. A semiconductor has a smaller gap, so heat or light can lift a few electrons across it.  ·  The working relations are A conductor has overlapping or partly filled bands and An insulator has a large gap. A semiconductor has a smaller gap. Name each symbol, convert the data into SI units, and only then substitute.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: When many atoms form a solid, interactions split atomic energy levels into closely spaced allowed bands separated by forbidden energy gaps. Electrons cannot occupy energies in an ideal band gap.  ·  The valence band contains bonding electrons; the conduction band contains mobile carriers. The gap Eg=Ec−Ev and the band filling help explain conductivity.  ·  ### Deep dive: bands, gaps and the conductor/insulator switch When N atoms bond into a solid, each atomic level splits into N closely spaced levels — effectively a continuous *band*. The valence band holds the bonding electrons; the conduction band is the first empty band where electrons can move freely.…

A photon of wavelength 800 nm has energy 1240/800 = 1.55 eV. Can it lift an electron across the gap?

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Metals have partially filled bands or overlapping bands. Insulators have a large gap and very few room-temperature carriers. Semiconductors have a smaller gap, so thermal or optical excitation can promote electrons into the conduction band.  ·  In an intrinsic semiconductor, promoting an electron leaves a hole in the valence band. Both the electron and the hole can carry current; heating can therefore increase carrier concentration.  ·  A photon can excite an electron across the gap if hν≥Eg. This underlies photoconductivity and semiconductor photodetectors.
